chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Abi al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Raqqi, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, from al-Hasan ibn Abdullah, from his forefathers, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both).

He said: A group of Jews came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and asked him, with the most knowledgeable among them asking questions. Among what they asked was: 'Why has God made fasting for thirty days during the day incumbent upon your nation, while He made it incumbent upon other nations for more than that?'

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, when Adam ate from the tree, it remained in his stomach for thirty days. So God, the Exalted, made it incumbent upon his offspring for thirty days: hunger and thirst. And what they eat is by God's grace upon them. Thus it was with Adam, so God made that incumbent upon my nation.'
Fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that you may become righteous.
God, the Exalted, said: 'For a fixed number of days.' The Jew said: 'You are right, O Muhammad.'
ai.seo_question: Why did God prescribe fasting for thirty days according to the explanation given to the Jews in this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Khisal* highlights the concept of *Tawfiq* (divine facilitation) and the symbolic connection between the first human, Adam, and the final Prophet, linking the duration of fasting to the time food remained in Adam's stomach. It underscores the continuity of divine law (*Shari'ah*) across prophets, a theme central to Shia theological discussions on the wisdom behind specific ritual durations. The Jew's affirmation serves as a witness to the prophetic truth, reinforcing the universal applicability of these divine ordinances.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 21-5 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil-Qasim quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of Abil Hassan Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Reqqi,on the authority of Abdullah ibn Jaballe, on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Ammar, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Abdullah, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of his grandfather Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB),

“Several Jews went to see the Prophet of God (MGB) and one of them asked him several questions which included the following question, ‘Why has God made it incumbent upon your nation to fast for thirty days while He has made it incumbent for other nations to fast for more days?’

The Prophet (MGB) said, ‘Indeed when Adam ate from the tree, the fruit remained in his stomach for thirty days before it was digested. That is why the Honorable the Exalted God made it incumbent upon his offspring to abstain from eating and drinking for thirty days. What they are allowed to eat and drink during these thirty days is due to the Honorable the Exalted God’s Nobility. God has imposed the same restrictions on my nation that He imposed on Adam (MGB).

Then the Prophet (MGB) recited the following verse, ‘Fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that ye may (learn) self-restraint,- (Fasting) for a fixed number of days;’
The Jew said, ‘O Muhammad! You are right!’”
